about: Every image asset Eldmoor wants (#177). npm run art:daily (scripts/art/daily.mjs) generates the missing ones in priority order through Hugging Face Inference Providers until the day's share of the monthly credits is used, into assets/incoming/<date>/ for review; npm run art:accept moves reviewed ones into assets/ and assets/index.json. Each asset has a procedural fallback (its hook); a missing file never breaks a world. Data only: no game code reads prompts.

schema.id: '<kind>:<name>', unique; name is lower-case letters, digits and '-'. The file is assets/<kind>/<name>.png.
schema.kind: tile | autotile | building | landmark | sprite | portrait | prop | icon (must equal the id's prefix)
schema.priority: a priorities[].n: the daily run makes lower numbers first, then manifest order
schema.sizes: {"32": [w, h], "64": [w, h]}: pixels after post-processing at each tier (src/render/tile.js TIERS); the renderer uses the tier of its TILE. One entry, one prompt and one seed for every tier, so a 64 set is a regeneration pass, not new design
schema.frames: sprite sheets only: {cols, rows}: frame columns (stand, step, other step) and rows (facing down, left, right, up); every tier's size splits into them
schema.model: optional key of 'models'; default: pinnedModel, else the first candidate that answers (recorded in assets/queue.json)
schema.prompt: what to draw; the model's trigger word and the top-level 'style' are added around it
schema.seed: integer, fixed so a regeneration is reproducible where the provider honours seeds (alternates and rejected redraws add an offset)
schema.palette: {from: [paths into src/render/palette.js exports, e.g. 'BIOME.meadow'], extra: ['#rrggbb', ...]}: the only colours the asset may use
schema.post: {fit: 'crop' (tiles: a seamless window of the model image at its own pixel scale) | 'scale' (shrink the subject), grid?: block size hint in px (default the model's grid, else 8), tone: bool (match the palette's tones, default true), dither: RGB amplitude of a 4x4 ordered dither (0 = none), minPalette: widen a short palette with shades to this many colours (6), minColors: an output with fewer colours is rejected as flat (default 4 for tiles, 2 otherwise), downscale: 'mode'|'mean' (scale fit), transparent: bool, bgTolerance: number, outline: bool, outlineColor?: '#rrggbb'}
schema.kindStyle: optional {kind: style}: replaces 'style' in the prompts of that kind (buildings and landmarks are not seamless ground)
schema.hook: {module: renderer file, export: the object in it that names this id with its procedural fallback, fallback: words}

priorities.name: terrain tileset (slice 2): base tiles per biome, road, water, transition edges, corners and inner corners, tree and rock variants
portrait library (slice 5): about 40 faces per people x class, picked by hash at founding

allowance.source: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/pricing (read 2026-11-03): free accounts get no Inference Providers credits, PRO $2.00 a month, extra use is pay-as-you-go. daily.mjs spends at most monthlyUsd / days-in-month a day and stops for the month at monthlyUsd. carry: a day that made nothing adds its share to the next days of the month (the loop, art:loop).

tiers.about: Generation settings per tier (src/render/tile.js TILE is the tier the renderer draws; art:daily and art:gen take --tier, default TILE). From the owner's three-tier comparison on 2026-11-03 (pixel-xl, same prompt and seed, LoRA scale 1.0 / 0.55 / 0.2, reduced to 128 / 256 / 512 px): the 32 tier sits near LoRA scale 0.55 with the model's pixel grid read as 4 px, the 64 tier near 0.2 with grid 2. A model's own tiers{} overrides these. minPalette widens each asset's palette with shades (src/render/palette.js TIER_SHADES).

style: top-down 2d game tile seen from directly above, 16-bit era JRPG overworld, crisp pixels, flat colours, no perspective, seamless

kindStyle.building: one building drawn alone in a 16-bit era JRPG overworld town, seen from above at a slight angle so the roof and the front wall both show, light from the top left, crisp pixels, flat colours
kindStyle.landmark: a set piece of a 16-bit era JRPG overworld seen from directly above, light from the top left, crisp pixels, flat colours

negativeStyle: text, watermark, signature, border, frame, photo, realistic, 3d render, blurry, gradient, perspective, isometric, horizon, sky

pixel-xl.why: Most-liked pixel-art model on the Hub (666 likes), an SDXL LoRA live on fal-ai through Inference Providers; its card advises downscaling by 8, which post-processing does.
pixel-xl.firstRun: 2026-11-03: answered 5 of 5 (estimate $0.01 an image; confirm on https://huggingface.co/settings/billing). Its tiles came out flat under the first post-processing; post-texture.mjs fixes that.

pixel-redmond.why: Second SDXL pixel-art LoRA on the same fal-ai route; a different look if the first is refused.

ume-flux.why: FLUX.1-dev pixel-art LoRA (MIT), live on fal-ai; better prompt following, dearer per image.

z-turbo.why: Z-Image-Turbo pixel-art LoRA (Apache-2.0), live on fal-ai; 8 steps, cheap.

flux-schnell.why: Last resort: a base model (no pixel LoRA) on fal-ai; the post-processing still forces the pixel grid and palette.

costNote: costPerImage values are estimates of what a call draws from the account's Inference Providers credits, not quoted prices. Credits are monthly ($2.00 on PRO, none on a free account); past them use is pay-as-you-go if the account has a payment method, so daily.mjs stops at its own budget (allowance) before relying on a 402.
